claims.evidence: The report confirms a rear derailleur exists but the number of gears on the cassette and crankset cannot be counted from the photo.
Photo 0 shows drop handlebars which typically house integrated or mounted shifters.
The frame material cannot be determined from a distance; welds or a magnet test are required.
Top speed depends on the rider and terrain, not just the mechanical state of the bike.

risks.risk: Structural frame damage (cracks or dents hidden by paint).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all frame joints and the underside of the down tube.
risks.if_unproven: as a damaged frame with scrap value only.

risks.risk: Worn or seized drivetrain (chain, cassette, derailleur).
risks.proof: A video of the pedals being turned and the gears shifting through the full range.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full drivetrain replacement.

risks.proof: A video of each wheel spinning freely to check for lateral wobble.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring wheel truing or replacement.

risks.proof: A video showing the seat post being adjusted/moved.
risks.if_unproven: as a fixed-size frame which limits resale value.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the brand name and model on the frame.
Close-up photo of the rear gears (cassette) to verify the speed count.
Video of the bike shifting through all 24 gears.
Close-up of the frame welds to confirm if it is aluminum or steel.
response.reason: The brand and model are unknown, and the frame material—which dictates the base value—cannot be verified from the current report.
